reason: E1 supports the expectation that NbTi-based HEAs may outperform Nb-Ta ones and that Ti-rich alloys show higher Hc2, but it does not provide evidence that lowering VEC enhances electron-phonon coupling or that disorder improves Tc; E2 mentions VEC trends but does not link them to the proposed mechanism. The key mechanistic premises about VEC, density of states, and disorder are thus largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: NbTi-based HEAs will have higher Tc/Hc2 than Nb-Ta-dominated type-A HEAs
Ti-rich ternary/quaternary Nb-Ti-X alloys show highest Hc2
Lowering VEC enhances density of states and electron-phonon coupling
Increasing Ti content introduces lattice disorder that modifies scattering and Tc/Hc2
Tc-VEC trends in HEAs differ from classical/amorphous alloys
